nodes.title: Knowledge gaps prioritised

content.title: Knowledge gaps prioritised
content.verifiable_criterion: The gap analysis is delivered and names, in priority order, the biodiversity knowledge gaps the three cases will address and the data each one needs.
content.source_ref: Call extract $.scope_requirements[1]; span SRC-WP9-P75#336-417

nodes.title: Architecture and joint protocols agreed

content.title: Architecture and joint protocols agreed
content.verifiable_criterion: The integration architecture, the case selection and the joint collection, metadata and processing protocols are all delivered, and every partner running a campaign has adopted the protocol in writing.
content.note: The gate before any campaign starts. A case run under a protocol that changes later produces data the other two cases cannot join.

nodes.title: All three campaigns running under the joint protocol

content.title: All three campaigns running under the joint protocol
content.verifiable_criterion: The terrestrial, freshwater and marine campaigns have each collected at least one field round, the omics sampling protocol is delivered, and the reporting-needs assessment states what the outputs must carry.

nodes.title: Training resource documented and the crosswalks published

content.title: Training resource documented and the crosswalks published
content.verifiable_criterion: The training and validation resource is published with its split protocol, and the crosswalk package resolves every habitat label the project uses to the European classification and the global typology.

nodes.title: Omics layer joined to the observation record

content.title: Omics layer joined to the observation record
content.verifiable_criterion: The molecular dataset, the genome-to-space linkage report and the processing pipeline release are delivered, and a molecular record can be joined to an in-situ and a satellite record through the published metadata.

nodes.title: Three realms delivered and the models benchmarked

content.title: Three realms delivered and the models benchmarked
content.verifiable_criterion: The three case datasets are delivered under one protocol, and the classification models report benchmark scores on each of them under the declared split.
content.note: The second scope requirement is answered here or not at all. Each realm rests on one partner, so losing P07 or P08 removes a realm rather than delaying it.

nodes.title: Cross-case verification complete and the indicators released

content.title: Cross-case verification complete and the indicators released
content.verifiable_criterion: The verification report states which harmonisation decisions survived transfer between realms and which did not, and the indicator decision-support release is available to the user network.

nodes.title: European coverage delivered and the exploitation route settled

content.title: European coverage delivered and the exploitation route settled
content.verifiable_criterion: The European-scale maps and trend predictions are published with stated uncertainty, the usability evaluation is reported, and the exploitation plan names the route each output takes after the project.

nodes.title: Build one multisensory integration architecture that carries omics, in-situ and remote-sensing observation on a single pressure gradient

content.title: Build one multisensory integration architecture that carries omics, in-situ and remote-sensing observation on a single pressure gradient
content.measurable_output: A prioritised knowledge-gap and data-need analysis, and an integration architecture specification covering the molecular, plot, airborne and satellite layers
content.source_ref: Concept note, 'The chain, from genome to space'; claims C01-C03 and C16 of project_summary.json
content.note: The gap analysis runs before the architecture, in the order the scope requirement states. The architecture is specified once and then tested three times, once per realm.

nodes.title: Agree joint data-collection, metadata and processing protocols, and publish them with crosswalks to the European habitat classification and the global ecosystem typology

content.title: Agree joint data-collection, metadata and processing protocols, and publish them with crosswalks to the European habitat classification and the global ecosystem typology
content.measurable_output: One protocol set adopted across the three cases, a crosswalk package, a provenance-tracked pipeline release, and publication to the open science cloud and the common data spaces
content.source_ref: Concept note, 'The chain, from genome to space' and 'Coordination the topic requires'; claims C08, C09, C15, C18 and C23
content.note: The scope asks the project to contribute to consensus, not only to comply. The contribution to the standards bodies is a task, not a dissemination line.

nodes.title: Turn the multi-season field archive and the case observations into documented training and validation resources

content.title: Turn the multi-season field archive and the case observations into documented training and validation resources
content.measurable_output: A published training and validation resource with a declared split protocol, in which site, season and treatment travel together into one fold
content.source_ref: Concept note, 'Training and validation data'; claim C06
content.note: The split protocol is the objective, not a detail of it. A resource whose folds leak the site teaches a model to recognise the site.

nodes.title: Run three demonstration and verification cases along one agricultural pressure gradient, across the terrestrial, freshwater and marine realms

content.title: Run three demonstration and verification cases along one agricultural pressure gradient, across the terrestrial, freshwater and marine realms
content.measurable_output: Three harmonised observation datasets, one per realm, and a cross-case report on which harmonisation decisions survived transfer between realms
content.source_ref: Concept note, 'Three demonstration cases on one gradient'; claims C04, C05 and C13
content.note: One gradient rather than three sites. A harmonisation decision taken for farmland is then tested in two realms that did not design it.

nodes.title: Deliver habitat and ecosystem classification and biodiversity trend prediction at case, regional and European scales

content.title: Deliver habitat and ecosystem classification and biodiversity trend prediction at case, regional and European scales
content.measurable_output: Benchmarked classification models for the three cases, European-scale habitat and ecosystem maps, and trend predictions with stated uncertainty
content.source_ref: Concept note, 'Training and validation data'; claims C07 and C17
content.note: Three scales, because the scope names three. The European scale rests on the case models, so it cannot be delivered before them.

nodes.title: Carry the validated indicators into policy reporting and into farm management, so biodiversity evidence reaches the sectors that create the pressure

content.title: Carry the validated indicators into policy reporting and into farm management, so biodiversity evidence reaches the sectors that create the pressure
content.measurable_output: A reporting-needs assessment agreed with competent authorities, an indicator decision-support release, and a usability evaluation run through a multi-country network of agricultural holdings
content.source_ref: Concept note, 'Reaching agriculture'; claims C10, C14, C19 and C20
content.note: The topic names agriculture twice, as a pressure and as a sector to reach. This objective answers the second naming.

capabilities: plant phenotyping under controlled and field conditions
content.role_in_the_action: Coordinator. Owns the in-situ physiological and metabolomic measurement chain, and the statistical design and validation protocol the whole data-integration chain is tested against.
Leads sensor harmonisation from field spectroscopy through aerial survey to satellite earth observation, which is the technical spine of the integration the topic asks for.

capabilities: multi-season controlled field-experiment archive covering physiological, spectral, soil-water and weather measurements
content.role_in_the_action: Supplies the long-run field archive that is reworked into documented training and validation sets, and the agricultural pressure gradient the demonstration cases run along.
Engineers the reproducible processing and provenance layer, and the decision-support surface the harmonisation workflows are delivered through.

capabilities: multi-country user network of agricultural holdings as an uptake channel
content.role_in_the_action: Carries biodiversity indicators into farm-management tools, which is how the project mainstreams biodiversity data into the agricultural sector the scope names.

Transfers the measurement protocols to a second production context and a second country, so the harmonisation is tested outside the setting it was built in. P06 held no in-action role in instance one and is a beneficiary here.

content.gap_closed: No freshwater expertise among the derived six, although the scope asks for capabilities across terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems.
capabilities: freshwater monitoring aligned with water-policy reporting
in-situ observation of floodplain and riparian ecotones adjoining farmland
content.role_in_the_action: Runs the freshwater demonstration case and the ecotone observations that connect the farmland pressure gradient to the water bodies receiving it.

content.gap_closed: No marine expertise among the derived six, and no partner able to contribute occurrence data to a marine data facility.
capabilities: coastal and benthic habitat mapping, including submerged vegetation meadows
marine indicator assessment for policy reporting
sub-orbital and ocean-colour earth observation of transitional waters
contribution of occurrence records to a global marine biodiversity data facility
content.role_in_the_action: Runs the marine demonstration case in coastal transitional waters, the downstream end of the catchment-to-coast chain, and carries the marine reporting indicators.

content.gap_closed: No genomic, transcriptomic or environmental DNA capability among the derived six. P01's metabolomics is their only omics layer, and the second expected outcome names all three.
content.role_in_the_action: Supplies the genomic and transcriptomic layer of the genome-to-space chain, and the omics metadata standard the integration is built on.

content.organisation_description: Non-profit research organisation, biodiversity data infrastructure
content.gap_closed: No biodiversity data-infrastructure partner among the derived six, so nothing to carry the cooperation with in-situ data collection frameworks, the typology crosswalks or the open-science-cloud link the scope requires.
capabilities: operation of a national species-occurrence data facility that publishes to a global biodiversity data facility
biodiversity data-standard crosswalks between occurrence standards, the European habitat classification and a global ecosystem typology
findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable metadata practice
integration of services into the European open science cloud
content.role_in_the_action: Owns the interoperability and data-publication layer: the crosswalks, the metadata profile, the cooperation with the named in-situ data frameworks, and the interface a Joint Research Centre contribution would attach to.

content.gap_closed: No socio-ecological or socio-economic analysis among the derived six, although the third scope requirement asks demonstration cases to take socio-economic pressures into account.
capabilities: socio-economic driver analysis for agriculture and aquaculture
policy-reporting needs assessment under the nature and habitat directives and the nature restoration regulation
content.role_in_the_action: Analyses the pressures the demonstration cases are selected against, and translates the reporting requirements the scope names into data needs.

content.organisation_description: SME, earth observation analytics and artificial intelligence
content.gap_closed: No partner among the derived six runs artificial-intelligence habitat mapping or trend prediction at European scale, which the first and third expected outcomes both require.
capabilities: deep-learning habitat and ecosystem classification from the European radar and optical earth observation missions
predictive biodiversity trend modelling at European scale
content.role_in_the_action: Scales the habitat and ecosystem classification from the demonstration cases to European coverage, and runs the trend prediction the first expected outcome names.

content.text: Horizon Europe - Work Programme 2026-2027 Food, Bioeconomy, Natural Resources, Agriculture and Environment Part 9 - Page 47 of 360 R&I actions under this destination will encourage international cooperation in line with the global approach on R&I, contributing to EU international biodiversity commitments, notably those taken under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF)79, which defines targets for the medium term (2030) and goals for the long term (2050). This destination will also support the Paris Agreement80, the Sustainable Development Goals81 and the United Nations agreement on biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement)82. Support to processes of the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES)83 will be continued. Complementarities and synergies will be ensured with the activities supported by the co- funded partnerships Biodiversa+ 84 , Water4All 85 and the co-funded partnership on Agroecology86, and LIFE87 projects, particularly on nature restoration and protection. The destination supports unlocking the unique assets for research and innovation of the EU outermost regions, in line with the EU strategy for outermost regions88. Expected impact: Proposals for topics under this destination should set out a credible pathway contributing to “putting biodiversity on a path to recovery, and protecting and restoring ecosystems and their services”, and more specifically to one or more of the following expected impacts: • Knowledge on biodiversity status and trends and drivers of biodiversity loss is improved; • Innovations, methods, pathways, models and tools are available and used to protect healthy and resilient ecosystems and to restore degraded ones, ensuring the continuous provision of ecosystem services, including for adaptation and/or mitigation to climate change; • The ongoing biodiversity crisis and its consequences, notably on ecosystem functioning and their services, and the need to monitor, protect, restore and sustainably use biodiversity are better understood to better benefit the whole society in an inclusive way; • Policymakers and stakeholders, all relevant economic sectors and society are aware and well informed of relevant challenges and opportunities of biodiversity protection, restoration and sustainable use, leading to better implementation of the biodiversity 79 Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework 80 The Paris Agreement | UNFCCC 81 THE 17 GOALS | Sustainable Development 82 BBNJ Agreement | Agreement on Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction 83 IPBES Home page | IPBES secretariat 84 Biodiversa + 85 Water Security for the Planet 86 Agroecology Partnership 87 LIFE - European Commission 88 COM(2022) Putting people first, securing sustainable and inclusive growth, unlocking the potential of the EU’s outermost regions

content.text: Horizon Europe - Work Programme 2026-2027 Food, Bioeconomy, Natural Resources, Agriculture and Environment Part 9 - Page 74 of 360 Research and Training Programme of the European Atomic Energy Community (2021-2025) 112. Expected Outcome: Project results are expected to contribute to all of the following expected outcomes: • advancing robust, policy-relevant ecosystem assessment, nature protection and restoration planning activities, and biodiversity trend prediction based on fit for purpose data, thus supporting EU biodiversity and climate objectives; • strengthened capacity of researchers, practitioners and decision-makers to improve biodiversity monitoring practices and address knowledge gaps via the integration of data and observations across sensors and platforms, ranging from omics-based data (genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic), various in-situ to satellite-based Earth observation data; • enhanced usability of in-situ datasets as training and validation resources for statistical, machine learning and advanced AI-based approaches, in support of applications such as habitat classification, ecosystem mapping and biodiversity trend prediction. Scope: Achieving the goals of the EU biodiversity strategy for 2030, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and assessing progress towards their defined targets, requires coherent, integrated and long-term monitoring approaches, underpinned by FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Re-usable) data systems. Many existing in-situ data collections (i.e. genomic assessments, ground sampling, drone and airborne observations) were not designed with Satellite Remote Sensing integration in mind (i.e. for validation and calibration, integrated data products, or statistical scaling of information) and lack the structure, interface and metadata required to support advanced analytics, including AI. FAIR data on species and ecosystems will also help to ensure that biodiversity preservation is a mainstream feature of other sectors, such as agriculture, transport, energy or the bioeconomy. There is a need for systemic, harmonised or standardised biodiversity data at Earth’s surface in order to support AI applications ranging from genome to space and to build up our knowledge on the status and trends of habitats, species, ecosystems, and on the drivers of decline. To address these challenges, proposals should: • develop and validate fit-for-purpose multisensory biodiversity data integration systems, to enable omics-based and in-situ data harmonization and integration with remote sensing data from space or sub-orbital platforms, as well as socio-ecological and climatic data for enhancing assessment of ecosystem condition and degradation, and the predictive modelling of biodiversity trends at international, regional and European scales; 112 This decision is available on the Funding and Tenders Portal, in the reference documents section for Horizon Europe, under ‘Simplified costs decisions’ or through this link: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/horizon/guidance/ls- decision_he_en.pdf

content.text: Horizon Europe - Work Programme 2026-2027 Food, Bioeconomy, Natural Resources, Agriculture and Environment Part 9 - Page 75 of 360 • develop concrete technical capabilities able to answer to diverse use cases, across terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems in Member States and Associated Countries. To this end, proposals should identify and prioritise critical biodiversity knowledge gaps and their data needs, with a focus on predictive analytics and the use of AI, and address them by designing data integration approaches that support scientific and policy needs, including biodiversity protection, restoration, and sustainable use goals and targets, as well as other related policy objectives; • develop demonstration and verification cases focusing on specific ecosystems under the EU ecosystem typology113 and habitats, including ecotones114, identified as those under pressure or as restoration priorities. Proposals should take into account socio-economic pressures and activities impacting ecosystems, including land and sea use and emissions of pollutants (e.g. agriculture, aquaculture, urbanization, resource exploitation and management practices). Demonstration cases should be relevant to EO applications, such as AI-assisted ecosystem and habitat mapping, ensuring interoperability with European and global frameworks such as the Global Ecosystem Typology as well as EUNIS, and aligned with reporting requirements under the Habitats Directive, Birds Directive, Marine Strategy Framework Directive and EU Nature Restoration Regulation; • deliver FAIR data, harmonisation workflows and processing protocols supporting data integration from genome to space and verify the use of generated datasets on identified analysis needs. Proposals should link observation data to emerging socio-economic, climate, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and environmental data and to relevant data infrastructures, including, if applicable, the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) and the European Common Data Spaces and SAGE115; • contribute to consensus and implementation of joint definitions of data collection, metadata and processing protocols, data quality and harmonization of standards enabling the integration of observations “from genomes to space”. Proposals should earmark resources for cooperation with existing initiatives such as in-situ data collection frameworks (e.g., GBIF, OBIS, LUCAS).The Joint Research Centre (JRC) may join the selected consortium in relation to effective coordination with the EC Knowledge Centre for Biodiversity (KCBD) and its Science Service, as well as incorporating the in-situ data from European Commission steered biodiversity monitoring schemes such as LUCAS, specifically LUCAS grassland, and EMBAL (European Monitoring of Biodiversity in 113 The “EU ecosystem typology” is a classification of ecosystem types developed by the Commission and the European Environmental Agency, in collaboration with Member States and it is tailored to meet EU needs. Its first level is legislated and is used for the reporting under in Annex IX of Regulation (EU) 691/2011. 114 Ecotones are areas of steep transition between ecological communities, ecosystems, and/or ecological regions along an environmental or other gradient.
